text: It is a nice room, she said as they climbed, and it is not often vacant, for I had some most elegant people in it last summer. <break time="0.8s" /> Sprowls and Mooney, a vaudeville act, kept it for three months, and Miss B aretta Sprowls had her marriage certificate framed and hung over the dresser. <break time="0.8s" /> Theater people mostly come here, sir, because this is the theatrical district, and actor people never stay long anywhere, she added, and he paid for a week in advance. <break time="0.8s" /> Then he asked the question that he had already asked a thousand times, Have you ever had a young girl named Eloise Vashner among your lodgers. <break time="0.8s" /> She is a fair girl of medium height, slender, with reddish gold hair and a dark mole near her left eyebrow, he explained, and she probably sings on the stage. <break time="0.8s" /> The housekeeper did not remember the name, saying that stage people change their names as often as their rooms, and that they come and they go. <break time="0.8s" /> For five months he had searched without rest, questioning managers, agents, schools, and choruses, and searching theaters from the finest stages down to the lowest music halls. <break time="0.8s" /> He had loved her best, and he was sure that she was somewhere in this great city, which, like a monstrous quicksand, kept shifting and swallowing everything without a trace.
